h1:
Where to Stay in Ratchaburi?
12 Hotels We Actually Reviewed
Prices Compared Across 3 Sites!
heroSub: 12 hand-picked Ratchaburi hotels across every budget — from resorts and villas in the Suan Phueng valley to Bali-style villas around Damnoen Saduak, a Mae Klong riverside boutique and budget stays in town. From roughly ฿450–7,500/night.
introH2: 🏞️ Why does choosing the right area in Ratchaburi matter so much?
introHtml: Ratchaburi packs mountains, floating markets and an old town into one province, and each area feels completely different. Suan Phueng is the mountain valley about 60 km from town — perfect for cool air and nature trips. Damnoen Saduak is the famous floating-market district on the eastern side of the province. The Mae Klong River stretch in town has riverside stays, while the Ratchaburi town centre is a convenient base near the market and the walking street. Many travellers book without checking whether they're on the Suan Phueng side or the Damnoen Saduak side, then end up driving 60–80 km across the province each day. This guide rounds up 12 Ratchaburi hotels hand-picked across every tier — each one with real guest-review feedback, prices compared across 3 sites, and direct booking links.
mrtHtml: Ratchaburi has no metro and no commercial airport — most people drive in from Bangkok in about 1.5–2 hours, or take a van/coach to the town centre. Hotels here are quite spread out, so pick by your itinerary: Suan Phueng is the mountain valley 60 km from town — easiest with your own car, with cool air, waterfalls and farms; Damnoen Saduak is the floating-market district to the east, ideal for the floating market and the Maeklong railway market; the Mae Klong River in town offers river views near the food streets; and the town centre is near the market, the walking street and Khao Ngu. Almost every hotel has free parking, so they suit self-drivers well.

entries.name: Villa Tuscany Country Resort
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Suan Phueng · in the valley · Ratchaburi
entries.addr: 439 Moo 1, Suan Phueng, Suan Phueng District, Ratchaburi
entries.storyHtml: Villa Tuscany is the most-reviewed resort in this guide — 330 reviews and a 9.0 score, and it's a Tuscan-style villa property in the Suan Phueng valley. Guests love the Italian look and feel, which is photogenic from every angle, the standalone villas that give real privacy, and the mountain views all around. At ฿1,200 for a Classic Villa it's great value for a private villa at this score, and there's free parking, so it suits self-drivers.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: for a clawfoot tub and full mountain views, pick the Villa Mountain View. Book ahead over the cool season and long weekends — rooms fill fast and prices climb.
pros: Photogenic Tuscan design from every angle
Standalone villas with real privacy
Mountain views all around, cool air
Great starting value for a private villa at this score
cons: Far from Ratchaburi town — a 60 km drive
Busy over long weekends, rooms fill fast

entries.name: Khum Damnoen Resort
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Tha Nat · Damnoen Saduak · near the floating market
entries.addr: 50/1 Tha Nat, Damnoen Saduak District, Ratchaburi
entries.storyHtml: Khum Damnoen is a Bali-style villa resort scoring a high 9.1. The standout is the 70-metre salt-water pool that guests rave about, Bali-styled villas — some with canal views — and a location near the Damnoen Saduak floating market, making market trips easy. The private-jacuzzi rooms suit couples celebrating a special occasion. At ฿2,150 to start, it's good value for a villa at this score in the floating-market area.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: for a waterside feel, pick a Lake Villa or Lake Jacuzzi with canal views. Celebrating an anniversary or honeymoon? Choose a private-jacuzzi room — and book ahead, as the villas fill fast.
pros: 70 m salt-water pool that guests love
Bali-style villas, some with pretty canal views
Near the Damnoen Saduak floating market
Private-jacuzzi rooms ideal for couples
cons: On the Damnoen Saduak side, fairly far from Suan Phueng and town
Villa prices are higher than typical stays in the province

entries.name: Rachabhura Hotel
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Mae Klong River · Ratchaburi town centre
entries.addr: 259 Moo 2, Ban Rai, Mueang Ratchaburi District, Ratchaburi
entries.storyHtml: Rachabhura is a 4-star riverside boutique hotel on the Mae Klong River in town, scoring 8.8. The standout is a design that draws on Ratchaburi's famous pottery heritage, warm clay-and-wood-toned rooms, and a riverside location right in town. There are pool-zone rooms and pool-access villas where you can step straight out to the pool. From ฿1,890, it's good value for a riverside boutique in town that's easy to get around from.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: to see the river, pick Superior Partial River View or above. To step straight into the pool from your room, choose Villa Pool Access. Reviews are still few as it's newly opened, but feedback on the design and cleanliness is strong.
pros: Ratchaburi pottery-inspired design, a real signature
Riverside Mae Klong location in town, easy to get around
Warm clay-and-wood-toned rooms, clean
Pool-zone rooms and pool-access villas
cons: Still few reviews (40), as it's newly opened
Standard rooms don't face the river — choose your room type

entries.name: Phu Pha Phung Resort
entries.badge: 🏊 Resort with a pool + family villas
entries.addr: 112 Moo 2, Suan Phueng, Suan Phueng District, Ratchaburi
entries.storyHtml: Phu Pha Phung is a 4-star Suan Phueng resort with a swimming pool and villas for larger groups, scoring 8.5. It suits families and groups of friends who want a resort with a pool at an accessible starting price. Guests like the spacious grounds, Suan Phueng mountain views, and the Family Studio and multi-bedroom villas that sleep several. At ฿1,100 for a garden-view double, it's good value for a resort with a pool.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: travelling as a group or larger family? Look at the multi-bedroom villas — split between you, they work out well. The Booking score sits a little below Agoda, so check recent photos and reviews before booking.
pros: Has a pool, at an accessible starting price
Multi-bedroom villas for larger groups
Spacious grounds, Suan Phueng mountain views
Free parking, suits self-drivers
cons: Booking score below Agoda; some rooms older than expected
In Suan Phueng, about 60 km from town

entries.name: The Scenery Vintage Farm & Resort
entries.badge: 🐑 Sheep farm · luxury villas · Suan Phueng
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Suan Phueng · in the valley · Ratchaburi
entries.addr: 234 Moo 7, Suan Phueng, Suan Phueng District, Ratchaburi
entries.storyHtml: The Scenery Vintage Farm is a luxury farm villa resort in the Suan Phueng valley and a landmark of the area, scoring 8.4. The draw is the sheep farm and English-Mediterranean villa setting that's photogenic all day, plus large villas with private jacuzzis or bathtubs. It suits anyone celebrating a special occasion or wanting a luxe stay in nature. At ฿7,500 to start it's the priciest in this guide, and you can book direct via the resort's own site.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: travelling as a family? Pick a Duplex Villa that sleeps 4 — split between you, it's better value. Book direct via the resort site, and book well ahead, as villas are limited and fill fast in the cool season.
pros: Sheep farm and villa setting, photogenic all day
Large villas with private jacuzzis / bathtubs
In the Suan Phueng valley — cool, private
Ideal for special occasions or a luxe nature stay
cons: Priciest in this guide, from ฿7,500
Deep in Suan Phueng — you'll need your own car

entries.name: Sleep by Me Ratchaburi
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Phetkasem Rd · Chedi Hak · near the town centre
entries.addr: 99/9 Moo 8, Chedi Hak, Mueang Ratchaburi District, Ratchaburi
entries.storyHtml: Sleep by Me is a boutique hotel in town scoring a high 8.6, from just ฿790. It's a renovated pink-toned building with an on-site café, photogenic and ideal for design lovers on a budget. Guests praise the clean rooms, comfy beds and friendly staff. It's in the Chedi Hak area near the town centre, easy to get around, with free parking — so it suits self-drivers.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: travelling as a family? Pick the Triple or Family Room for 3–4 guests. It's a town stay, not in Suan Phueng — allow driving time if you plan to explore the nature side.
pros: Renovated pink building with a café, photogenic
Clean rooms, comfy beds, high review scores
Very good starting value for the quality
Near the town centre, free parking
cons: In town, not in the Suan Phueng nature zone
Standard rooms are sleep-focused, not loaded with amenities

entries.name: Phu Ingthara Resort
entries.badge: ⛺ By a stream/waterfall · domes & stone houses
entries.addr: 549 Moo Huai Phak, Suan Phueng, Suan Phueng District, Ratchaburi
entries.storyHtml: Phu Ingthara is a nature boutique resort in Suan Phueng with both dome tents and design-led stone houses, scoring 8.4 from 120 reviews. The standout is its setting by a stream and waterfall, the nature-camp vibe, and a range of stays from budget domes to photogenic art-style houses. From ฿950 for an air-conditioned dome tent, it suits campers who want to sleep in nature but still have air-con.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: on a budget and OK with shared bathrooms? Pick a dome tent. Want an en-suite and waterfall views? Choose a stone / Hobbit house. Check which room type is en-suite before booking.
pros: By a stream and waterfall, deep in nature
Wide range of stays, from domes to art-style houses
Stone houses and design homes are photogenic
Accessible starting price for campers
cons: Cheaper dome tents use shared bathrooms outside
Deep in Suan Phueng; parts of the access road are unpaved

entries.name: Kao Ngu Boutique Resort
entries.badge: 🐾 Pet-friendly · at the foot of Khao Ngu
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Khao Ngu · Ko Phlapphla · Mueang · Ratchaburi
entries.addr: 292 Moo 1, Ko Phlapphla, Mueang Ratchaburi District, Ratchaburi
entries.storyHtml: Kao Ngu is a boutique resort at the foot of Khao Ngu that welcomes pets, from just ฿590, scoring 8.0. The standout is that it's one of the few pet-friendly stays in the area, with mountain views and a spot near Ratchaburi town that's easy to get around from. Rooms range from Standard up to Family. The Agoda score is a high 9.1 while Booking is 7.6, so check recent reviews and room photos before you book.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: travelling with a pet? Let the resort know ahead. For mountain views, pick a Superior Room. Cheap and near town, it makes a handy base for Khao Ngu and the town centre.
pros: Welcomes pets — rare near town
Khao Ngu mountain views, near Ratchaburi town
Very budget-friendly starting price
Several room tiers, including a Family Room
cons: Booking score notably below Agoda
A small resort, so amenities are limited

entries.name: The Bed Boutique House
entries.addr: 168 Moo 1, Chedi Hak, Mueang Ratchaburi District, Ratchaburi
entries.storyHtml: The Bed Boutique House is a budget in-town boutique hotel from just ฿450, scoring 7.9. It suits travellers on a budget who just want a clean room in town with free parking. Rooms range from a single-bed Mini Room to a Villa for a small family, with several non-smoking options. Reviews are still few (8), but feedback on cleanliness and value is good — a solid overnight stop.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: staying a few nights or as a couple? Pick the Twin or VIP Room, which is roomier than the Mini Room. It's a clean, budget sleep-stop rather than a resort with lots of facilities.
pros: Very budget-friendly, from ฿450
Clean rooms, several non-smoking options
Free parking, in Ratchaburi town
Good value as an overnight stop
cons: Very few reviews so far (8)
Mini Rooms are small and sleep-focused, few amenities

entries.type: Cottage resort in an elephant camp · 2-star
entries.name: Chang Puak Resort Damnoen Saduak
entries.badge: 🐘 Inside an elephant camp · Damnoen Saduak
tags: 🛶 Near the Damnoen Saduak floating market
entries.addr: 76/2 Moo 2, Khun Phithak, Damnoen Saduak District, Ratchaburi
entries.storyHtml: Chang Puak Resort is a cottage resort set inside an elephant camp in the Damnoen Saduak area, scoring 7.2. The draw is the experience of staying in an elephant camp that kids love, and a location near the Damnoen Saduak floating market. Rooms are single-storey cottages with air-con, hot water, TV and Wi-Fi, plus a Family Room that sleeps 3. It suits families who want their children near the elephants and a floating-market trip.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: travelling with kids? Pick the Family Room that sleeps 3. It's a stay inside an elephant camp — more about the experience than luxury, so expect a camp atmosphere and check the elephant-activity schedule before you go.
pros: The experience of staying in an elephant camp — kids love it
Near the Damnoen Saduak floating market
Private cottages with air-con and hot water
Has a Family Room, good for families
cons: Middling review scores, some about upkeep
Focused on the elephant-camp experience, not a luxury resort

entries.name: Tid-jai Homestay at Suan Phueng
entries.badge: 💧 By a stream · camping allowed · budget
entries.addr: 242 Moo 2, Tanao Si, Suan Phueng District, Ratchaburi
entries.storyHtml: Tid-jai Homestay is a streamside homestay in Suan Phueng for budget nature lovers. It's a set of small houses by a stream with a friendly homestay vibe, plus a camping area at just ฿150 per person. It suits anyone who wants to fall asleep to the sound of water in nature without needing luxury. Reviews are still few (2), but it scores 8.0, with good feedback on the atmosphere and friendly hosts.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: want air-con? Pick the air-con small house; the fan version is cheaper but uses shared bathrooms. Campers can pitch by the stream. Contact the homestay ahead, as space is limited.
pros: Houses by a stream — sleep to the sound of water
Camping allowed at a very low price
Friendly homestay atmosphere
Great for nature lovers on a budget
cons: Very few reviews so far (2)
Shared bathrooms and basic facilities

entries.name: Guest House Ratchaburi
entries.addr: 8/1 Moo 9, Don Tako, Mueang Ratchaburi District, Ratchaburi
entries.storyHtml: Guest House Ratchaburi is the cheapest stay in this guide, from just ฿550, scoring 6.5. It's a cabin-style guesthouse with a garden around the property, in the Don Tako area of Mueang district. It suits very budget-conscious travellers who just want an air-conditioned room at the lowest price; some rooms have a balcony looking onto the garden. Scores are middling and facilities basic, so check recent photos and reviews before booking.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: step up to a Standard Room with a balcony so you can sit and look onto the garden. It's a very budget stay — expect basic facilities, best for a single-night stop.
pros: Cheapest in this guide, from ฿550
Garden around the property, quiet feel
Some rooms have a garden-view balcony
Free parking, in Mueang district
cons: Middling review score (6.5)
Basic facilities, a budget sleep-stop

faqTitle: FAQ — Common traveller questions about Ratchaburi hotels

faq.q: ❓ Where should I stay in Ratchaburi — Suan Phueng or the town?
faq.a: It depends on your plan. For nature, mountains, waterfalls and cool air, pick Suan Phueng (Villa Tuscany, Phu Pha Phung, The Scenery, Phu Ingthara, Tid-jai), about 60 km from town. For the floating market, choose Damnoen Saduak (Khum Damnoen, Chang Puak). To stay in town near the food streets and walking street, pick the Ratchaburi town centre (Rachabhura, Sleep by Me, Kao Ngu, The Bed, Guest House).

faq.q: ❓ How much do Ratchaburi hotels cost?
faq.a: There's a wide range: budget stays and guesthouses in town start around ฿450–800/night; 3-star boutique resorts run roughly ฿900–2,200; 4-star villas and resorts are about ฿1,100–4,800; and a luxe villa like The Scenery starts around ฿7,500 and up. Over the cool season and long weekends, Suan Phueng rates run higher than usual.

faq.q: ❓ Can I visit Ratchaburi without my own car?
faq.a: Yes, if you stay in town. In Ratchaburi town you can grab a ride and walk to the market, the walking street and Khao Ngu easily. But to reach Suan Phueng, 60 km away, or the Damnoen Saduak floating market, your own car is much more convenient, as public transport is infrequent. The Suan Phueng and Damnoen Saduak stays in particular suit self-drivers.

faq.q: ❓ Which site is cheapest for booking Ratchaburi hotels?
faq.a: Prices on each site (Agoda, Booking.com, Trip.com) vary with each platform's promotions, so it's worth comparing all three before you book — every review page in this guide has price-comparison links, which can save several hundred baht a night. Some Suan Phueng villas can be cheaper booked direct via the resort's own site.

faq.q: ❓ When is the best time to visit Suan Phueng, Ratchaburi?
faq.a: The cool season (Nov–Feb) is the most popular — pleasant cool air, great for villa stays with a mountain breeze, and pretty flower fields and farms — but it's busy and rooms fill fast, so book ahead. In the rainy season the streams and waterfalls run beautifully, though some nature trails can get slippery. The hot season is quieter and cheaper.

faq.q: ❓ What is there to do in Ratchaburi?
faq.a: Ratchaburi has plenty to do. Suan Phueng has mountains, waterfalls, the sheep farm at The Scenery and viewpoints. Damnoen Saduak has the Damnoen Saduak floating market and the Maeklong railway market. The town centre has Khao Ngu, cave temples, the dragon-jar pottery and the walking street. It makes a great weekend trip from Bangkok — just a 1.5–2 hour drive.
